Our work spans Medicare Advantage, fully integrated care models, primary care, care for the most medically and socially complex populations, and next\-generation care delivery models. Across all of this, we are united by a shared commitment: combining compassion with discipline, innovation with stewardship, and growth with integrity.

**JOB DESCRIPTION**  

  

  

Wealth Planning \& Advice is a group of experts in trusts \& estates, tax planning, financial planning and planning in related areas for individuals and their entities (operating businesses, private foundations, etc.). Our role is to work with advisors and their clients to educate them about wealth planning opportunities both simple (e.g., asset titling, beneficiary designations) and complex (e.g., GRATs, split\-interest trusts). We provide intellectual capital to clients across the wealth continuum and will work one\-on\-one with clients in appropriate circumstances. Familiarity with the taxation of entities and of estates and trusts is also useful but not required. Knowledge of issues relating to securities\-based compensation (restricted stock, employee stock options, performance share units, etc.), pre\-liquidity planning, and concentrated position management (such as 10b5\-1 plans, derivative\-based transactions, and exchange funds) will also be a plus.


As the Executive Director, Wealth Planner within J.P. Morgan Wealth Management, you will leverage your deep understanding of tax and trust \& estate laws to communicate complex information in a simple, non\-technical manner to both clients and advisors, as well as field leadership. You will adopt a goal\-oriented approach when engaging with clients, which involves familiarizing yourself with the various investment, banking, and lending products and platforms available to our advisors across J.P. Morgan Wealth Management. This knowledge will enable you to identify issues and opportunities for client engagement. Additionally, you will collaborate with field management to develop regional strategies and provide guidance on their execution. A natural curiosity for people, planning, and the wealth management industry, along with independent initiative and responsiveness, are essential qualities for success in this role.


**Job Responsibilities:**


* Work with divisional leadership and WP\&A leadership to develop and present content across different wealth management topics.
* Serve as a resource to the JPMWM field in the areas of both simple and sophisticated tax and trust \& estate planning strategies as well as in concentrated position management, corporate executive services, and pre\-liquidity transaction planning.
* Partner with field leadership and Practice Management to integrate estate and tax planning concepts into goals\-based advice.
* Maintain up\-to\-date knowledge of both federal and state tax laws relating to our areas of focus.
* Promote J.P. Morgan's knowledge and sophistication to outside centers of influence, primarily accountants and attorneys.
* Work with Advisors to develop business opportunities with new and existing clients.
* Provide unbiased comprehensive and customized wealth planning advice to clients and prospective clients.
* Work with individuals across the entire wealth spectrum and have experience with tax and wealth transfer strategies.
* Actively participate in team discussions to proactively propose planning ideas and industry trends that can be shared with the field.
* Travel to local and out of state branches, as needed.

**Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills:**


* 4\-year college degree and either J.D, LLB, CPA or CFP
* 7 plus years of practice as a trusts \& estates lawyer, tax advisor, or financial planner
* Knowledge of issues relating to securities\-based compensation (restricted stock, employee stock options, performance share units, etc.), pre\-liquidity planning, and concentrated position management (such as 10b5\-1 plans, derivative\-based transactions, and exchange funds.
* Must be comfortable working with individuals across the entire wealth spectrum and have experience with tax and wealth transfer strategies; familiarity with financial planning, investments, and corporate executive issues.
* Ability to drive business results with broad background in trust and estate planning issues.
* A strong self\-motivated individual who can work closely with Advisors without daily contact with a direct manager.
* Strong presentation skills in one\-on\-one and group meetings
* Experience and ability in understanding clients' financial situations and personal circumstances
* Must be able to coach colleagues, Financial Advisors and clients (very strong partnership skills)
* Individual with high ethical standards who never sacrifices integrity and works in the clients' best interest

**Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills:**


* Series 7 \& 66 required (may be fulfilled within 4 months of assuming role)
* Familiarity with financial planning, investments, corporate executive issues and concentrated stock management is a plus
* 10b5\-1 plans, derivative\-based transactions, and exchange funds, and concentrated stock management is a plus
* Experience with financial planning software a plus

FEDERAL DEPOSIT INSURANCE ACT:


This position is subject to Section 19 of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act. As such, an employment offer for this position is contingent on JPMorganChase's review of criminal conviction history, including pretrial diversions or program entries.


**ABOUT US**  

  

  

Chase is a leading financial services firm, helping nearly half of America's households and small businesses achieve their financial goals through a broad range of financial products. Our mission is to create engaged, lifelong relationships and put our customers at the heart of everything we do. We also help small businesses, nonprofits and cities grow, delivering solutions to solve all their financial needs.


We offer a competitive total rewards package including base salary determined based on the role, experience, skill set and location. **Aunt Lute Books Co\-Executive Director in Administration Job Posting**

**About the Organization**

Aunt Lute Books is a 44\-year\-old non profit, intersectional feminist press dedicated to publishing literature by writers who have traditionally been underrepresented or excluded from the literary canon. For more than four decades, Aunt Lute has championed bold, boundary\-pushing fiction, to create space for voices and perspectives too often marginalized within mainstream publishing.

**About the Position**

Aunt Lute is seeking a motivated and collaborative **Co\-Executive Director in Administration** to help co\-lead the organization through its next stage of growth and sustainability. This part\-time position (20\-22 hours per week) works in partnership with the Co\-Executive Director in Operations. The Co\-Executive Director in Administration will focus primarily on fundraising, grant writing and resource development, financial oversight, organizational growth and strategic planning, community engagement and Board relations. They will uphold Aunt Lute’s mission and values in their leadership and decision\-making. This is a hybrid position based in San Francisco. Ideally, candidates should be able to work in\-person once a week and attend events.

*\*See Addendum below for Co\-Executive Director in Operations responsibilities.*

**Job Responsibilities:**

Development

* In collaboration with the Board of Directors, creating and implementing fundraising plans that primarily focus on private foundations and individual annual donors.
* Working closely with staff and Board to accomplish revenue goals consisting of major gifts, foundation and government grants.

Financial Management

* Having a daily knowledge of where financial matters stand for the organization, which includes providing transparent fiscal stewardship that maintains a positive financial position and adequate control and accounting of all funds.
* Develop and propose an annual budget to the Board for their approval.
* Working with our accounting consultant to reconcile accounts and to write tax reports including city, state, and federal reports as required.

Organizational Growth

* With the Board of Directors, creating short\- and long\-term strategic plans in support of Aunt Lute’s mission and documenting progress towards achieving them.
* Developing and improving organizational infrastructure, including business processes, systems, policies, and tools, to maximize efficiency and future growth.

Community Engagement/Outreach

* Participating in relevant community events and cultivating speaking skills to deepen local networks, engage new donors, and expand community presence.
* Developing and nurturing positive relationships with other arts and cultural organizations.
* Supporting staff in planning and executing events sponsored by Aunt Lute in partnership with mission\-aligned organizations.
* Practice feminist leadership styles and ability to engage with racial/gender equity organizations.

Staff Management

* Work with the Co\-ED in Operations to manage the recruitment, employment, and release of all personnel while implementing sound human resource practices.
* Co\-managing the oversight of employee performance and delegating responsibilities.
* Promoting a work culture that is inclusive, equitable, transparent, and respectful of all backgrounds and identities.

Board Relations

* Support the board in recruiting and identifying prospective members who bring diverse skills, perspectives, and strong commitment to Aunt Lute’s mission.
* Maintaining regular communication with the Board Chair through regular check\-ins, and attending and supporting preparation for Board meetings, held every other month to advance organizational priorities and implement strategic planning.
* Providing leadership in developing program, organizational, and financial plans with the Board.

**Required Skills for this Position:**

Required skills and qualifications:

* 3 or more years in non\-profit organizational management within publishing, literary arts, or cultural organizations
* 3 years of experience in managing budgets; considerable experience working with spreadsheets (Microsoft Excel)
* Experience in grant writing, fundraising, and donor relations
* Demonstrated commitment to equitable and transparent collaboration with colleagues
* Highly competent in verbal, written, and visual communication
* Proximity to or ability to commute to the Bay Area for in\-person meetings and events

Preferred skills and qualifications:

* Experience working with a nonprofit Board of Directors
* Experience with fundraising tech platforms
* Knowledgeable with Social Media and Publicity
* Experience with QuickBooks

**Compensation:**

* $34\-$38/hour for 20 hours per week

**How to Apply:** 

Email a resume and cover letter addressed to Aunt Lute Search Committee to jobs@auntlute.com*.* 

Cover letters should address how applicants believe their qualifications, experience, aspirations, and values align with Aunt Lute’s publishing mission. Review of applications will begin on November 1, 2026, and applications will be accepted until the position is filled. If selected for an interview, candidates will be asked to complete an online questionnaire and provide references.

**\*Addendum**

**The Co\-Executive Director in Operations is responsible for:**

* Accounts payable, receivable, banking, and account reconciliation
* Working with the accountant on account reconciliation and end of the year reporting.
* Reporting to the accountant as they close the financial year: on payroll, inventory, sales, etc.
* Payroll and related financial reporting
* Book inventory management, reprints, and shipping
* Serving as liaison with Aunt Lute’s distributor, Ingram
* Overseeing royalty calculations
* Coordinating logistics for book fairs, events, and conferences
* Reporting to the Board on forthcoming book releases, sales, cash and investments, and other operational matter

We are seeking an energetic, exceptional Chief Operating Officer to oversee the day\-to\-day operations of our complexes throughout the United States and help drive the company’s continued growth and success. Reporting directly to Ownership, the COO will translate strategy into disciplined execution, strengthen operational systems and leadership capacity, and ensure the organization operates safely, efficiently, and cost\-effectively.

**Key Responsibilities**

· **Set enterprise production standards:** Establish clear expectations for production, cost, quality, safety, delivery, and operational discipline across all complexes.

· **Direct daily operational execution:** Set priorities, allocate resources, approve operating plans, resolve execution issues, and ensure leadership teams operate with urgency and discipline.

· **Drive accountability:** Hold leaders and teams accountable for schedules, cost targets, production goals, quality standards, safety performance, and delivery commitments. Establish clear performance expectations, address issues promptly, and take corrective action through coaching, restructuring, or personnel decisions when required.

· **Intervene decisively:** Act quickly when performance, discipline, or results deviate from expectations by directing corrective actions, changing operating approaches, or making leadership changes necessary to restore performance.

· **Convert strategy into execution:** Turn strategic initiatives into clear plans with defined owners, timelines, performance expectations, and measurable outcomes.

· **Align capital and operations:** Strengthen the connection between strategic objectives, capital deployment, production capacity, capacity planning, improvement initiatives, and approved investment strategies.

· **Deliver executive visibility:** Provide Ownership with clear insight into company operations, project performance, financial trends, organizational capacity, and emerging risks.

· **Prepare the organization for scale:** Strengthen leadership systems, processes, management depth, and organizational structure to support sustainable long\-term growth.

· **Develop leaders:** Build and lead high\-performing teams; develop future executives, project leaders, and field leaders; and foster collaboration, innovation, inclusion, and alignment with company values and goals.

**SCHEDULE:** **2027\-28 School Year – Full\-time**

**WAGE:** **$****125,000 to $166,61****1**




**Nevada City School of the Arts \- Executive Director Job Posting**


Nevada City School of the Arts is seeking an experienced, mission driven leader to serve as its next Executive Director.

**About NCSA**
--------------


Nevada City School of the Arts is a tuition\-free public charter school in California, providing students, families, and staff with an arts based choice for elementary education. NCSA fosters academic, artistic, and social emotional achievement, serves as a collaborator and contributor to the greater community, and is committed to safe, respectful, and equitable conditions for learning and working for everyone in our community.


NCSA is located in Nevada City in the Sierra Nevada foothills, a small, arts rich community with a strong sense of place and civic involvement.

**Enrollment and grades served:** TK\-8, 517 students

**Staff:** 108

**The Position**
----------------


The NCSA Board of Directors, Charter Governance Council, is seeking a highly qualified and dedicated Executive Director to lead Nevada City School of the Arts and advance its mission and vision.


The Executive Director serves as NCSA's chief executive and provides strategic, instructional, organizational, fiscal, personnel, and facilities leadership. The position is responsible for supporting academic excellence, arts integration, student well being, an inclusive and collaborative school culture, and the continued growth and success of NCSA.


The role also includes executive oversight and long term stewardship of NCSA's school owned campus and facilities, including facilities planning, deferred maintenance, capital improvements, and major projects.

**The Leader We Are Looking For**
---------------------------------


NCSA is seeking an experienced educational and organizational leader who understands the unique character of an arts integrated charter school and can provide strong leadership while preserving and strengthening the qualities that make NCSA special.


The successful candidate will demonstrate:

* A strong commitment to NCSA's mission, vision, and arts integrated educational philosophy.
* A successful record of educational and organizational leadership.
* Experience leading teachers, administrators, classified employees, and other professionals in a school setting.
* Strong instructional leadership and a commitment to academic, artistic, and social emotional achievement.
* Strong financial management skills, including budgeting, forecasting, resource allocation, and long term planning.
* The ability to lead a complex organization, establish priorities, delegate effectively, develop strong teams, and follow through.
* Experience overseeing complex facilities, long term facilities planning, deferred maintenance, capital improvements, or comparable organizational assets.
* The ability to navigate difficult issues, manage competing priorities, build consensus, and lead an organization through change.
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills and the ability to build relationships with students, staff, families, the Board, and the broader community.

**The Opportunity**
-------------------

  

The Oklahoma Tobacco Settlement Endowment Trust seeks an exceptional executive leader to serve as its Executive Director and lead one of Oklahoma's most distinctive public institutions.  



  

Created by a vote of the people of Oklahoma in 2000, TSET is entrusted with converting the certified earnings of the state's tobacco settlement endowment into strategic grants that improve the health and well\-being of Oklahomans. Through statewide programs, community grants, research, and evidence\-based initiatives, TSET works to and create lasting improvements in the health of Oklahoma communities.  



  

The Executive Director reports to the TSET Board of Directors and serves as the organization's chief executive, strategic leader, and principal administrative officer, responsible for translating the Board's vision, policies, and priorities into effective strategy, disciplined execution, and measurable results.  



  

This is more than an administrative leadership position. The Executive Director must lead at the intersection of public policy, public health, government, grantmaking, organizational management, and Board governance, and must understand how to operate effectively within a politically complex environment while preserving TSET's institutional integrity, credibility, statutory responsibilities, and long\-term mission.  



  

The successful candidate will bring exceptional executive judgment, political acumen, strategic thinking, financial stewardship including a comprehensive understanding of the financial statements of TSET, communication skill, and relationship building ability, equally comfortable advising a governing Board, leading a professional staff, engaging senior state leaders, working with public and private grantees, evaluating grant proposals, and representing TSET before diverse constituencies across Oklahoma.  



  

TSET's founders built this organization twenty\-five years ago in the truest entrepreneurial sense, establishing its systems, its credibility, and its impact largely at the same time it was already operating. Today, TSET enters a different season: a mature institution with a substantial endowment, an established track record, and significant resources to direct toward growth and innovation. The next Executive Director will need real leadership maturity: the ability to assess what the Board of Directors of TSET wants the Trust to become, recognize what has earned its place, and lead the organization through thoughtful renewal where it is warranted, bringing the same resourcefulness that built TSET together with the institutional discipline this next chapter demands, including an assessment of the necessary cultural changes to accomplish the future direction of TSET  



**About TSET**
--------------

TSET is a constitutionally protected public trust and, at the same time, a state agency, a grantmaker, a public health institution, and a steward of tobacco settlement certified earnings, governed by an appointed Board of Directors. By constitutional design, only the certified earnings on the Trust's investments, may be spent, and those earnings are directed toward clinical and basic research and treatment efforts in Oklahoma for the  



  

purpose of enhancing efforts to prevent and combat cancer and other tobacco\-related diseases, cost\-effective tobacco prevention and cessation programs, and other health related initiatives.  



  

**Vision and Mission:** Improving the health of every Oklahoman.  



  

TSET's giving is guided by five core principles: prioritizing evidence based and proven approaches; encouraging innovative and creative solutions; fostering collaborative relationships to maximize efficiency; supporting comprehensive services across both urban and rural Oklahoma; and awarding funding based on merit and public benefit. In practice, current strategic priorities span tobacco cessation, cancer research, healthcare access, workforce development, and prevention.  



  

TSET holds assets of approximately $2 billion and ranks among the state's largest health focused grantmakers, supporting roughly 100–150 active grants each year, typically $50,000 to $5 million per award, to universities, health systems, and community organizations. Signature initiatives include the Legacy Grants program, which awarded a combined $150 million to 14 grantee organizations, announced in 2025, and research grants, and efforts to promote tobacco cessation.  



**Governance**
--------------

TSET's governance is divided between two boards. A separate, five\-member Board of Investors, chaired by the State Treasurer, is constitutionally responsible for investing the Trust's assets. The seven\-member Board of Directors does not invest the endowment; rather, it directs the certified earnings that the assets generate toward constitutionally authorized health programs, research, and administration. The Executive Director leads the agency that converts those earnings into public impact.

Bordering Southeast Florida’s Atlantic coastline, Broward County is the seventeenth most populous county in the nation and the second largest in the state of Florida. Broward County boasts 23 miles of pristine Atlantic coastline, and its beaches attract both the local population as well as tourists from around the world. With an average year\-round temperature of 76 degrees, Broward County has a tropical climate and is a choice destination for over nineteen million visitors every year.
  

  

Broward County’s warm climate, demographic diversity, robust and expanding economy, top\-rated schools, colleges and universities, cutting\-edge healthcare, and an advanced transportation system afford its residents an exceptional quality of life. Broward offers world\-class dining, high\-quality theater, cosmopolitan nightlife, and premium shopping venues, as well as an abundance of recreational activities such as golf, pickleball, soccer, deep\-sea fishing, boating and vast opportunities for fun on the beach.

The Broward County government was established under Charter in 1975 as a home\-rule government. The County has a Council/Manager form of government. Commissioners are voted to the position by their district constituents through partisan elections. The Mayor and Vice\-Mayor are Commission members annually elected by the Commission for one\-year terms. The Commission appoints the County Administrator, the County Attorney, and the County Auditor.

The County has nearly 6,700 employees and eight organized bargaining units. The existing public transportation network provides approximately 26 million fixed route and express service bus trips annually. This belief is lived through a model that combines rigorous academics with strong relationships and student agency. Every student has a dedicated mentor who serves as a consistent advocate and bridge between school and home. Through Next Prep, a core Kairos program focused on self\-discovery, career exploration, and professional skill\-building, students develop a clear plan for life after graduation and build the skills to pursue their education, income, and life goals. Students also connect their learning to the real world through job site visits, networking, professional skills practice, paid internships, and other college and career experiences.


In 2026, Kairos celebrated one of its most significant milestones to date: graduating its first senior class. This achievement marks an important moment in Kairos’s continued growth and reflects its commitment to preparing students to thrive in the lives they choose after graduation.


As Kairos moves beyond its founding years, the organization enters its next chapter with meaningful momentum and a clearer understanding of where it must continue to grow. About Evergreen Goodwill
  
  

Evergreen Goodwill of Northwest Washington is a 501(c)(3\) nonprofit organization founded in 1923 that helps people get jobs across Northwest Washington by offering high\-quality free job training, education and job placement. Goodwill empowers individuals to overcome barriers to working, by providing comprehensive support and connecting them with life changing job opportunities, ensuring they are career\-ready and can support themselves and their families.
  
  

The organization employs over 2,000 people, operates five job\-training centers, 23 nonprofit retail stores and more than 27 donation sites in King, Snohomish, Skagit, Whatcom and Kitsap Counties. Every day, Evergreen Goodwill connects people with the jobs, services and skills they need — because Jobs Change Lives. We are committed to creating and sustaining a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion (DEI) and are focused on creating a joyful, inclusive and successful organization.
  
  

**Job Title:** Executive Director, Evergreen Goodwill Education Center
  
**Location:** Evergreen Goodwill Job Training \& Education Center \- Seattle, WA
  
**Salary Range:** $180,000–$220,000
  
  

Evergreen Goodwill is seeking a Founding Executive Director to build and lead the Evergreen Goodwill Education Center (EGEC), a new organization formed to operate Washington State’s first adult high school using the Goodwill Education Initiatives model. Over the next decade, the Evergreen Goodwill Education Center plans to launch at least five Excel Centers—public high schools for adults ages 18 and older—in King, Snohomish, Skagit, Whatcom, and Kitsap counties. Washington’s Excel Centers will build on the national Goodwill Excel Center model, which now includes 50 campuses across 11 states and Washington, D.C. The model combines rigorous academics, wraparound services, and life coaching to help adult students earn high school diplomas.
  
The Executive Director will shape the execution strategy, build the organization, launch its schools, beginning with Excel Center Goodwill Dearborn in Seattle, and lead them toward long\-term success.
  
We are looking for an executive and builder who can define a bold strategy, translate it into action, and deliver on the promise of these schools. This leader will build and inspire a team, deliver strong student outcomes, engage funders and community partners, advocate for the schools, build an effective board and collaborate with its members, and create a financially and operationally sustainable institution.
  
About The Excel Center
  
The Excel Center model is a tuition\-free public high school designed to help adults earn a state\-recognized diploma, not a GED, along with college credits or industry certifications. Flexible schedules, life coaching, childcare, and transportation support help students balance school with work and family responsibilities. Excel Center graduates earn more than a diploma: they gain college credits and professional certifications that open doors to higher\-paying careers in high\-growth fields. A University of Notre Dame LEO study of the Excel Center model in Indiana found that, five years after graduation, graduates earn 38% more and are significantly more likely to work in fields with career pathways, such as healthcare.
  
Evergreen Goodwill will bring the model to Washington and build on it. We aspire to open an Excel Center in each of the five counties where we operate, ultimately reaching 1,000–1,500 students within the next decade. The founding Executive Director will benefit from a proven model and significant training, guidance, and ongoing support from Goodwill Education Initiatives (GEI), the national experts behind The Excel Center, while shaping the school to meet the needs of our local community. A combination of public funding, including charter school funding, and private philanthropy will support the school.
  
**Learn more about the national Excel Center model:** https://www.goodwillexcelcenter.org/
  
  

**Five key functions of this role include:**  

1\. Academic Excellence, Curriculum Oversight, and Student Outcomes
  
2\. Culture, Talent, and Organizational Leadership
  
3\. Student Recruitment, Enrollment and Retention
  
4\. Partnerships, Board Engagement, Fundraising, and External Leadership
  
5\. Financial Management, Compliance and Accountability
  
What You’ll Do
  
* Build and lead the Evergreen Goodwill Education Center organization. You’ll hire and supervise the Excel Center principals and help build a team that includes teachers, special education and language teachers, coaches, a registrar, and an office manager. You’ll build the school culture, academic program, operations, systems, and infrastructure and put strong academic leadership and expertise in place to support the educational program.
* Shape the operational and growth strategy for the Excel Centers in Washington, translating a proven national model into exceptional public high schools for adults ages 18 and older that are responsive to their local communities.
* Set ambitious goals for enrollment, persistence, graduation, and postsecondary success, using data and accountability to drive strong student outcomes.
* Ensure the financial and operational health of the organization and its schools by overseeing budgeting, staffing, resource allocation, accreditation, charter requirements, and regulatory compliance.

Labcorp is a global leader in laboratory services, providing the insights and answers that help healthcare providers, patients, researchers, pharmaceutical companies and health systems make confident decisions and improve outcomes. Through our unparalleled science, data, technology and laboratory network, we advance diagnostics, accelerate innovation and help address some of the world’s most important health challenges. As we shape the future of healthcare, we are leveraging advanced technologies, intelligent digital solutions and data\-driven innovation across our operations to enhance how work gets done and deliver greater value to customers and patients. With our global scale and deep expertise, you’ll have the opportunity to do meaningful work, grow your career and make a real impact on people’s health around the world. Together, we’re improving health and improving lives.

  

Labcorp is seeking a National Program Director, Community Health Centers to join our team.

 **Responsibilities:**

* Own and execute Labcorp's national strategy and value proposition for Community Health Centers, HCCNs, and Primary Care Associations.
* Build and manage strategic partnerships with national HCCNs to advance contractual relationships and drive collaborative growth initiatives.
* Serve on NACHC Strategic Alliance team, leading workflow for member Best Practices and Toolkit development.
* Standardize and scale CHC services and programs across all operating Divisions.
* Lead development and commercialization of products, programs, and solutions that improve UDS and VBC quality measures, operational performance, and patient outcomes.
* Define Community Health Center pricing strategies and build consistency in how we approach uninsured populations and flat\-rate programs.
* Ensure CHC requirements are incorporated into specialty\-testing and value\-based care initiatives.
* Collaborate with Diagnostic Assistant, Insight Analytics, and data teams to enhance customer offerings and drive utilization.
* Partner with Divisional sales and leadership to support CHC growth and retention.
* Drive internal alignment on CHC strategy and lead cross\-functional teams in launching and scaling new programs and solutions.
* Serve as a subject matter expert for customer presentations, leadership discussions, and sales strategy
* Develop a centralized capability for CHC RFP responses and enable Primary Care Association engagement, and value\-based care contracting.
* Drive sales team communications, training, tools, and support resources.
* Lead targeting campaigns and sales enablement programs.
* Leverage laboratory data to support UDS quality measures, care gap initiatives, population health programs, and value\-based care performance.
* Lead Salesforce account hierarchy and data governance for CHCs, improve targeting and reporting.
* Drive customer\-facing communications in partnership with Marketing, including sales collateral, marketing campaigns, thought leadership, and CHC conference strategy and support.
* Monitor CHC segment performance through revenue, accession volume, and customer analytics.
* Present strategic updates, KPIs and market insights to senior leadership.
* Participate in business reviews with Divisional and national commercial leadership.
* Support commercial efforts to achieve annual CHC growth budget.

 **Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree
* 8\+ years’ experience in healthcare, laboratory services, public health, product management.

 **Additional Job Standards:**

* Experience working in lab services
* Product/Program Director experience in healthcare
* Laboratory, healthcare product sales or program management experience
* Experience with Community Health Centers (FQHCs) or large provider organizations
* Demonstrated ability to take a concept from inception to execution into the market
* Excellent communication skills with examples – marketing communications experience or advanced degree a plus
* Broad skill set with ability to think strategically (write a plan) and executive tactically (project management). Quantitative and communication skills are also critical for success
* Experience working with Community Health Centers, large provider networks, public health organizations.
* Strong understanding of Community Health Centers, laboratory testing, population health, and value\-based care models.

 **About the Role**


The **National Program Director of Community Health Centers** is responsible for leading Labcorp’s commercial execution for Community Health Centers (CHCs), working with cross functional teams to drive product development, supporting divisional sales success, and building strategic partnerships with national Health Center Controlled Networks (HCCNs). This role has primary responsibility for CHC national strategy, value proposition development, performance tracking, product and program implementation, pricing models, data and analytics solutions, industry partnerships, and sales enablement.


The National Program Director of Community Health Centers serves as Labcorp’s primary internal and external advocate for Community Health Centers, mobilizing cross\-functional teams across Sales, Managed Care, Marketing, IT, Legal, and Medical and Scientific Affairs to accelerate growth and strengthen Labcorp’s market position.


The National Director of Community Health Centers reports to the Vice President of Physician Systems within the National HHS Team.
